subject: Biology
title: What Is a Virus?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is a Virus?.

hook.text: A virus is just genetic code wrapped in a protein shell. It can't eat, grow, or reproduce alone.

buildup.text: To replicate, a virus hijacks a living cell and forces it to make copies of the virus.

discovery.text: Viruses are far smaller than bacteria—most are between 20 and 300 nanometers.

twist.text: Scientists still debate whether viruses are truly alive. They sit on the edge of life.

climax.text: Despite their simplicity, viruses have shaped evolution, driven pandemics, and changed history.

punchline.text: Not quite alive, but deadly effective.

quiz.question: Why can't viruses reproduce on their own?
options: They need a host cell's machinery
They are too large to divide

details.summary: Viruses are submicroscopic infectious agents consisting of genetic material, either DNA or RNA, enclosed in a protein coat. They cannot reproduce independently and must hijack living cells to replicate. Whether viruses are truly alive remains one of biology's most debated questions.
details.whyItMatters: Viruses cause diseases from common colds to pandemics, shaping human history and evolution. Understanding viral biology is essential for developing vaccines, antivirals, and gene therapy tools that repurpose viral mechanisms.
takeaways: Viruses are 20 to 300 nanometers, far smaller than most bacteria
They cannot replicate without hijacking a living host cell's machinery
Viruses exist on the boundary between living and non-living matter

faq.question: Are viruses alive exactly?
faq.answer: Viruses lack metabolism, cannot reproduce independently, and have no cellular structure. However, they evolve through mutation and natural selection, and replicate using genetic material. Most biologists consider them non-living but acknowledge they exist in a gray zone.

faq.question: How are viruses different from bacteria?
faq.answer: Bacteria are living cells that metabolize and reproduce independently. Viruses are much smaller, have no cellular machinery, and require a host cell to replicate. Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses. Different strategies are needed for each.
